scores.note: Restates his explicit refusal to villainise Simone; captures only the outward-empathy half, not the self-silence that pairs with it.
Lumps the Capelinha detour in with dignity-protection, which misreads its actual function as site-avoidance.
Correctly refuses the 'pushes her out' decoy, but the sabotage is something he already confesses himself.
Retells the robbery as a compliment; adds no pattern he couldn't read off his own story.
Gets the worry-into-measurement mechanism but only in the one episode where he already narrates it; misses that counting is where fear goes generally.
Names the give-and-conceal move but only from the sofa story; no cross-episode pattern, mostly reframing E2.
Cleanly identifies the two-decade repetition of loss-site avoidance dressed as errand logic; strongest version of this observation.
He states this mechanism verbatim himself ('it was a task'); the insight adds framing, not discovery.
Generic dignity-of-work reading; true of most people who tell this kind of story.
Love-as-logistics is accurate but is exactly what he narrates and what Bete teases him for.
Notices the unacknowledged night-to-morning switch as fear rather than scheduling — a real catch, though the headline pattern is stated loosely.
Rehearses the 'everything's resolved' joke and the brother-comparison he makes out loud in E5.
Grief-into-competence is his own account ('I got old in one week'); hedged with 'may' and no new specificity.
Good pickup on the reframed schedule change, but the belief stated is close to what he already knows about himself.
He says 'I know exactly what I did and I did it anyway'; this is a paraphrase of his own confession.
Correctly separates stated convenience from actual avoidance; weaker than x007 since it only gestures at the repetition.
Duty-after-loss is the known headline of E1, restated as a value.
First half restates; the 'never lets anyone protect him' claim sits awkwardly against Bené, Aparecido and the hall light he is in fact watched over by.
Elegant phrasing of an insight he delivers himself in E2 ('I understand it now').
Plausible transmission story from Bené, but the 'gift for ministry' claim is speculation he couldn't verify.
Assembles all three concealed sacrifices and names hunger-first-then-hide as one move; the sharpest capture of this pattern.
Notices that care always arrives unrequested via older men who don't ask questions — consistent with how his friendships actually work.
Rests on his own admission; the link to the ambulance-route arithmetic is asserted rather than earned.
Gets giving-plus-concealment from one episode; 'sacrifice itself is meaningful' overreads a man who calls it a task.
Mostly restates the bus story; the aside about the unnamed real reason for the shift change is the only added value.

scores.fp_reason: Contradicted by behaviour: he confesses the sleeping as something shameful, refuses the day off, and cannot rest unless it is disguised or stolen.
scores.note: Reads one wry line as a theology of unearned grace, inverting his actual relationship to rest.
Frames the counting as a competence strength rather than as displaced feeling, so it lands on the known self-description.
He explicitly says the not-asking was why he went; the generalisation to 'his definition of love' is mild extension.
Tracks the repeated phrase well, but he already knows it's a reflex and a family joke; 'neediness invites disaster' is asserted causation.
Quotes his own stated mechanism; the extension to finishing the line after the robbery is a small genuine addition.

scores.fp_reason: Factual error: conflates Bené (the elderly retired driver from church) with his brother Wellington, who was the one who died young.
scores.note: The central evidential claim misidentifies who died, so the whole reading is built on a mistake.
Humour-as-shield is plausible and lightly supported, but generic and hedged throughout.
Another pass at the same catchphrase; adds the pastor refusals but no new mechanism.
Joins the physical detours to the narrative cover stories as one avoidance grammar, which is the more general form of the pattern.
